about: Who may call which academy MCP write tool, and who owns which ticket field. Agents are named bare (the namespace is stripped by agent_identity); bare names are unique across the five plugins. The human (the main session, no agent_type) may do everything. Read tools (claims_show/list/query/deps, library_*, queue_status/log, env_*, domain_get, config_get, workspace_get, tickets_list/get, packets_list/get) are open to every caller and are not listed. The server checks the substance of each call on top of this table (docs/protocol.md).

claims_new.substance: Status must be unsettled (open, conjectured, sketch). The id must be in the caller's own instance namespace, except for claim-keeper. A claim created by researcher:generalize has status conjectured and bears_on the lab claim it generalizes.

claims_attach_evidence.substance: Append-only: an evidence row is never edited or removed. Grader verdicts reach the registry as files landed by a SubagentStop hook and are attached by claim-keeper or review-chair, never by the grader.

claims_propose_status.substance: Files a ticket (kind decision) to the claim-keeper of the claim's namespace owner; changes nothing itself.

claims_set_status.substance: The server re-checks the grounds per kind (plan section 8, registry/core/grounds.py): proof -> two agreeing verdicts with distinct run ids, graders other than the producer (grader_role != producer_role), and the claim's current statement hash; computation -> two agreeing experiment verdicts with distinct run ids and graders other than the producer, the result's commit hash and a passed validation case, and only supported/refuted/refuted-as-stated; or the human's word, quoted verbatim (basis human). Without grounds only the human may set a status. The change is applied by the registry engine (line-preserving) and refused if the record would then fail its check.

queue_add.substance: The script must be committed; the env profile defaults to the home's policy.run. The job file is built by scientist/scripts/env.py. Dry run (nothing written, the job file returned) unless the lab's academy.json sets scientist.queue.mcpAdd to on.

tickets_create.substance: from is the caller's instance (the human files as 'human', and the concierge files as 'human' only after Roey confirms); to must be a workspace instance or 'human'; the server allocates id and dates and writes status open.

tickets_update.substance: Field ownership and transitions per 'tickets' below; the caller's party (sender/receiver) is decided by its instance against the ticket's from/to. Appending to the thread is open to every non-readonly caller.

packets_create.substance: The packet's instance is the caller's instance; ## Summary, ## Established vs assumed and ## Decisions needed must be present and ## Decision empty. Read-only agents' packets (referee, rigor-reviewer) are landed by their SubagentStop hook, not through this tool.

packets_decide.substance: Only the human decides. /academy:review runs in the main session; the script writes the answer into the packet's ## Decision and a line into its ticket's thread.

tickets.human: Any field, any transition between valid statuses, including re-opening a terminal ticket to open.

files.about: Direct file edits guarded by hooks (not MCP). The hooks read this block.

board.note: Agents change the board only through the MCP tools; the human may edit in VS Code, and ticket_edit_check validates the result.
